name: Theoretical Chemistry
tagline: Quantum models, molecular orbital theory, and first-principles calculations.
seo_title: Theoretical Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Theoretical Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in quantum chemistry, density functional theory, bonding theory and reaction dynamics.

definition.lead: Theoretical chemistry uses mathematics and physics to explain chemical behaviour, and often to predict it before any experiment is run.
definition.body: Its central tool is quantum mechanics: describe the electrons correctly and you obtain bond lengths, energies, colours and reaction barriers. It builds the theories that computational chemistry turns into software.

facts.label: Dirac: the laws of chemistry are known; the equations are just too hard to solve exactly
Nobel Prize to Kohn and Pople for density functional theory and quantum chemistry methods

branches.name: Quantum chemistry
branches.summary: Solving the Schrödinger equation for molecules.
branches.example: Predicting bond energies and molecular geometries.

branches.name: Molecular orbital theory
branches.summary: Electrons spread over the whole molecule in orbitals.
branches.example: Explains benzene's stability and oxygen's magnetism.

branches.name: Valence bond theory
branches.summary: Bonds as overlapping atomic orbitals, with resonance.
branches.example: Pauling's hybridization explains carbon's tetrahedral shape.

branches.name: Density functional theory
branches.summary: Computing the energy from the electron density instead of the wavefunction.
branches.example: The workhorse method in materials and catalysis research.

branches.name: Statistical mechanics
branches.summary: From molecular energy levels to temperature, pressure and entropy.

branches.name: Reaction dynamics
branches.summary: How atoms move across potential energy surfaces during a reaction.
branches.example: Crossed molecular beam experiments test these predictions.

branches.name: Symmetry & group theory
branches.summary: Symmetry decides which orbitals mix and which transitions are allowed.

branches.name: Molecular dynamics
branches.summary: Newton's laws applied to every atom over time.
branches.example: Simulating how proteins move and fold.

timeline.title: The electron-pair bond
timeline.text: Gilbert N. Lewis proposes that a covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons.
timeline.why: The picture behind every Lewis structure.

timeline.title: The Schrödinger equation
timeline.text: Erwin Schrödinger describes electrons as waves.
timeline.why: Made it possible to calculate chemistry from first principles.

timeline.title: The first quantum bond
timeline.text: Walter Heitler and Fritz London treat the hydrogen molecule with quantum mechanics.
timeline.why: The first explanation of why a covalent bond forms.

timeline.title: Dirac's challenge
timeline.text: Paul Dirac writes that the laws of chemistry are known, but the equations are too complicated to solve exactly.
timeline.why: Set the agenda: find clever approximations.

timeline.title: Hückel's theory
timeline.text: Erich Hückel develops a simple orbital model for conjugated and aromatic molecules.

timeline.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
timeline.text: Linus Pauling publishes his book on bonding, hybridization and electronegativity.
timeline.why: One of the most influential chemistry books ever written.

timeline.title: The Roothaan equations
timeline.text: Clemens Roothaan, and independently George Hall, recast molecular orbital theory as matrix equations.
timeline.why: Turned quantum chemistry into something computers could do.

timeline.title: Density functional theory
timeline.text: Pierre Hohenberg and Walter Kohn show that the electron density determines all ground-state properties.
timeline.why: Now the most widely used electronic-structure method.

timeline.title: Frontier orbitals
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Kenichi Fukui and Roald Hoffmann for theories of chemical reactions.
timeline.why: Showed that a few key orbitals steer most reactions.

timeline.title: Multiscale models
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Karplus, Levitt and Warshel for models of complex chemical systems.
timeline.why: Combined quantum and classical physics to simulate enzymes.

quiz.q: Solving the Schrödinger equation for a molecule gives…
options: The allowed energies and wavefunctions of its electrons
quiz.explain: From energies and wavefunctions, nearly every other property can be derived.

options: Nuclei move much more slowly than electrons
Electrons do not repel each other
quiz.explain: Nuclei are thousands of times heavier, so electrons can be solved for with the nuclei held fixed.

quiz.q: Density functional theory computes the energy from…
quiz.explain: The density depends on 3 coordinates, while a wavefunction depends on 3 per electron.

quiz.q: Which hybridization does the carbon in methane have?
quiz.explain: Four equivalent sp³ orbitals point to the corners of a tetrahedron.

quiz.q: In molecular orbital theory, bond order equals…
quiz.explain: For H₂: ½ × (2 − 0) = 1, a single bond.

quiz.q: Why do the HOMO and LUMO matter so much?
options: Most reactions involve the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied orbitals
They are the only orbitals with electrons
quiz.explain: Fukui's frontier orbital idea: reactivity is mostly decided at the edge of the electron distribution.

quiz.q: Who wrote 'The Nature of the Chemical Bond'?
quiz.explain: Published in 1939, it introduced generations of chemists to hybridization and electronegativity.

quiz.q: According to the Pauli exclusion principle, one orbital can hold at most…
quiz.explain: No two electrons may share all four quantum numbers.

quiz.q: The variational principle says a trial wavefunction's energy is…
options: Never lower than the true ground-state energy
Always lower than the true energy
quiz.explain: So lowering the energy of a trial function always moves it toward the truth.

quiz.q: The 1998 Nobel Prize to Kohn and Pople recognized…
options: Density functional theory and computational quantum chemistry
quiz.explain: Kohn developed DFT; Pople built methods and software used by chemists everywhere.

options: Energy as a function of atomic positions
quiz.explain: Reactants and products are valleys; the transition state is the mountain pass between them.

quiz.q: Which molecule did Heitler and London treat in the first quantum theory of a bond (1927)?
quiz.explain: The simplest molecule with a shared electron pair.
